In upstream proxy mode, the CONNECT request sent to the upstream proxy now brackets IPv6 literals in its authority. I didn't run anything, and I didn't add a test.

The change is in `mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/_upstream_proxy.py`, in `HttpUpstreamProxy.start_handshake`. The authority was built as `host:port` with no brackets, so a target like `::1` produced `CONNECT ::1:443`, which is ambiguous and invalid. If the IDNA-encoded host contains a colon, it is now wrapped in `[...]`, giving `CONNECT [::1]:443`. The `Host` header, when `http_connect_send_host_header` is on, reuses the same authority, so it is bracketed too. `request.host` is unchanged.

I skipped the test because `test_upstream_proxy` in `test/mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/test_http.py` is built around the domain-name cases. Covering IPv6 there means handling a bracketed CONNECT from the client too, which I didn't want to write without running it.
